faqs.a:
(a)
Impoundment.
The filing of charges is not a prerequisite for the impoundment of an animal.
(1)
Generally.
An animal management officer may impound an animal when:
(i)
There is probable cause to believe that the animal or its owner or custodian is in
               violation of a provision of this chapter or in violation of a state statute or regulation
               related to the care, custody, or treatment of animals; or
(ii)
An animal dies or is found dead on public property or on property other than that
               of the owner or custodian.
(2)
Other circumstances.
Subject to the availability of resources needed to properly and humanely impound
               an animal, an animal management officer must impound an animal when it:
(i)
Presents a clear and present danger to the public's health, safety, or welfare;
(ii)
Is found to be injured on public property or property other than that of the owner
               or custodian without permission of the property owner;
(iii)
Is owned or kept by a person who has been adjudged a habitual offender under
section 14-11
when there is probable cause to believe that the animal or its owner or custodian
               is in violation of a provision of this chapter or in violation of a state statute
               or regulation related to the care, custody, or treatment of animals;
(iv)
Is found to be running at large and whose owner or custodian is subject to a third
               or subsequent violation within any one-year period of
section 14-54
, running at large, relating to that or another animal;
(v)
Is an animal the keeping of which is prohibited under
section 14-91
, certain animals prohibited; or
(vi)
Is owned by, or being kept, harbored, or cared for by a person who is or has been
               detained or arrested if it reasonably appears to the officer that the detainee or
               arrestee is unable to immediately provide a responsible alternate custodian for the
               animal.
(b)
Care and provision; costs.
An animal management officer may consult with a veterinarian as to the disposition
               of an ill or injured impounded animal if the animal's prognosis cannot be ascertained
               by the officer with reasonable certainty. The officer may transport an impounded animal
               to a veterinary care facility for stabilizing veterinary treatment, to an animal care
               facility designated by the city as its animal shelter, otherwise arrange for the care
               of and provision for the animal, or otherwise arrange for the animal's disposition.
               The officer may arrange for a necropsy for an animal with written consent of the owner
               of the animal, if known, or upon issuance of a warrant signed by a judge. The owner
               or custodian of the impounded animal will be liable for all impoundment fees, disposal
               fees, veterinary expenses, and other costs for the care of and provision for the animal
               as set forth in this article.
(c)
Animal to be made available.
If at the time a determination to impound an animal is made in a case where an owner
               is cited for a violation of
section 14-51
, dangerous animals,
section 14-52
, aggressive animals,
section 14-91
, certain animals prohibited,
section 14-171
, cruelty,
section 14-171.5
, neglect, or
section 14-174
, care of animals, or in a case where the owner or custodian has been deemed to be
               a habitual offender under
section 14-11
, the subject animal is not made available to the animal management officer at the
               time of the issuance of a summons and complaint, the owner must produce the animal
               within 24 hours of the issuance of the summons and complaint at a time and place to
               be designated by the animal management officer.
(d)
Rabies observation.
Impoundment or confinement of an animal for rabies observation will be as set forth
               elsewhere in this chapter.
(e)
Impoundment of wild animals.
Notwithstanding any other provision of this article, an animal management officer,
               at their discretion, may apprehend any wild animal that is at large within the city,
               that is ill or injured such that the most humane course of action is to impound the
               animal, that is causing damage to property, or that constitutes a hazard to the public.
               The animal may be impounded, released to appropriate caregivers or keepers, relocated,
               or destroyed at the sole discretion of the animal management officer, subject to applicable
               provisions of the laws of the state.
(
Ord. No. 4878
, § 9, 10-7-2024)
